title: Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection via Prototype-Based Distillation
claim: A frozen teacher guides a mixture of students through a shared prototype space, with losses stabilizing and aligning their outputs.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right, three shaded zones, loss equations on dashed loops
description: A wide architecture diagram split into three soft-colored regions. The top-left green region, labeled Pre-trained Teacher, shows a small input graph G=(A,X) feeding a snowflake-marked self-supervised GNN. The GNN outputs a hidden vector, which passes through a flame-marked Adapter to give z_i^t. The bottom-left blue region, Mixture-of-Students, takes node features and node residuals into a Router. The Router dispatches to a shared student S^g and several local students S^l_1..S^l_N, whose outputs are weighted and summed into h^g and h^l. The right orange region, Prototype Space, shows two stacked tilted planes with colored prototype clusters. One plane takes the teacher output and the other takes the student outputs. Each plane feeds a soft-label bar chart (q and s), and a vertical dashed arrow between the charts carries the Distillation Loss KL formula. Dash-dotted loops carry the Commitment and Refinement Loss equations. Flame icons mark trainable modules and the snowflake marks the frozen one. The eye goes first to the top-left graph, then follows the arrows right.
caption: The architecture of the ProMoS. During training, a frozen self-supervised GNN teacher guides a Mixture-of-Students via prototype-guided soft-label distillation, while discrepancy-aware commitment and refinement objectives stabilize teacher outputs and refine the prototype for cross-graph consistency. During inference, anomalies are identified by fusing distillation bias with geometric deviation, enabling zero-shot detection on unseen graphs.
abstract: Driven by the pressing demand for graph anomaly detection (GAD) in high-stakes domains, the generalist GAD paradigm, which trains a single detector transferable across new graphs, has recently gained growing attention. However, existing methods often rely on scarce and costly annotations for training and sometimes even require few-shot support at inference, which limits their robustness to diverse and unseen anomaly patterns. To address this limitation, we introduce ProMoS, the first unsupervised generalist GAD framework, which detects anomalies by modeling the abundant normality in unlabeled data. ProMoS adopts a knowledge-distillation paradigm to distill normality priors from a frozen self-supervised graph neural network (GNN) teacher to a mixture-of-students model with shared global and lightweight personalized branches, enabling efficient and expressive normality modeling without learning from scratch. We further propose prototype-guided soft-label distillation to align teacher and student in a shared prototype space, enhancing cross-graph generalizability. During inference, ProMoS performs zero-shot anomaly detection on unseen graphs via distillation bias and prototype geometric deviation. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness and efficiency of ProMoS, charting a practical path toward label-free, zero-shot generalist GAD.
